finding: The client approves and the agency's Review panel keeps saying nobody has replied — the last step of the whole agency job renders the waiting state forever.
evidence: ReviewTab branches on round.status ONLY for changes_requested (ReviewTab.tsx:683); there is no APPROVED branch anywhere in the file (grep 'round.status' → :683 only). getCurrentRound returns the LATEST round whatever its status (review.service.ts:311-313, findFirst({where:{siteId}},orderBy createdAt desc) — no status filter), and fetchCurrentRound passes it straight through (ReviewService.ts:209-213). An APPROVED round with no client comments therefore falls to the `total === 0` arm (ReviewTab.tsx:685-686) and renders emptyBody — "{reviewerName} has not commented yet. You will be notified." (ReviewTab.tsx:629-636), which is board 157:221's copy. Section 1776:8383 contains no approved board: a TEXT scan of all 23 boards for /approv|closed/i returns only 157:169's history rows ('Round 6 · approved 3d ago'), 158:213's toast string, and Compare's label.
fix: Add an APPROVED arm to the body chain in ReviewTab.tsx:681-689 (approvedBody: '{reviewerName} approved this design' + resolvedAt + the next move), and draw the board it renders. Board 158:213's stated contract is stronger — panel gone entirely — so decide which of the two is the design before building.

finding: The two sections that make up the agency workflow are not joined in either direction: no board in 18 · Review reaches the client experience, and no board in 19 · Client sign-off returns to it.
evidence: Full-page inbound-edge scan of 1:3: the only edge into 1339:7162 from outside section 19 is 129:223 'S5.1 · sent' via hotspot 1671:7275 (section 23 Journeys). Board 156:2's own 16 reactions go to sibling Review states, 817:5069 (share permissions) and 52:2 (back to editor) — none to 1339:7162. Outbound from 1339:7186 (D · approved) is a single reaction, 1672:7201 → 1340:7174 (E). Nothing in section 19 points into section 18. So the prototype can walk agency→states and client→states but never agency→client→agency, which is the loop the module exists to describe.
fix: Add a hotspot on 156:2 (and/or 158:213) → 1339:7162 labelled 'what the client sees', and a hotspot on 1339:7186 → the approved Review-panel board created by W-E-01/W-E-16.

finding: B · commenting is a dead end that also deletes the sign-off buttons: the board drops the sticky footer, so a client who starts writing is shown a screen with no way to approve.
evidence: Layer tree of 1340:7162: children are 1340:7163 'Agency header', 1340:7165 'Site preview (iframe)', 1340:7166 'Your notes' — no footer node. Boards 1339:7171 (A) and 1340:7174 draw the footer with 'Request changes' + 'Approve this design'. In code A and B are the SAME render: the footer is on Shell for every PENDING round (review-client.tsx:281-305) and does not depend on whether a note is being typed. Reactions on 1340:7162: exactly one, 1671:7315 hotspot/back → 1339:7171. There is no B→C and no B→D edge.
fix: Copy the sticky footer group from 1339:7171 onto 1340:7162, and add hotspots 1340:7162 → 1339:7193 and → 1339:7186 mirroring 1671:7311 / 1671:7313.

finding: The agency board groups client comments by page ('OPEN · HOME', 'MENU') but the client page can never attach a page or an anchor to a comment, so every real client note lands in one 'General' group.
evidence: clientCommentInput accepts pageId, x, y and targetSelector (packages/shared/schemas/reviews.ts:98-107) and createClientComment persists all four (client-review.service.ts:232-244). review-client.tsx sends only {token, body} — at :336-337 for 'Add note' and at :437-438 in the request-changes path. It structurally cannot do more: the snapshot renders in an iframe with sandbox="" (review-client.tsx:70), so no click inside the reviewed page is observable. On the agency side pageName(null) returns 'General' (ReviewTab.tsx:233-240) and rowMeta prints it (:555), and the group header is `Open · ${g.label}` (:733). Board 156:2 draws 'Sara · client · Home · 2d' and a 'MENU' band; the shipped panel will print 'Sara · client · General · 2d' for every client comment.
fix: Either give the client page a pin affordance (a page selector at minimum — pageId needs no iframe interaction), or redraw 156:2's client rows without page attribution so the panel is not designed around data the client half cannot produce.

finding: DEAD — the census's single candidate, the 'Look at {Site}' CTA on A0, is a submit button for a form the board does not draw.
evidence: 1339:7169 [FRAME] 'CTA' rel@444,412 392x40 inside card 1339:7166 (rel@420,176 440x300); the card's only other children are 1339:7167 (heading) and 1339:7168 (body, ends ~rel y280), leaving 132px of empty card where the inputs belong. It carries no reaction, and the board's four hotspots sit at rel y682 and y820 — outside the 720px board, per the file's legend convention — so nothing overlays it either. In code the equivalent button is type="submit" on a form whose two required inputs it exists to submit (review-client.tsx:199-239).
fix: Rides on W-E-06 — draw the name and email fields in the gap; the CTA is then correct as drawn. Do not wire the CTA itself; the file's convention is legend hotspots.

finding: The identify board draws neither of the two fields the client must fill in, and the whole sign-off flow gates on them — the echo lost the form its canonical parent has.
evidence: Layer tree of 1339:7166 'Card': 1339:7167 heading, 1339:7168 body, 1339:7169 CTA. No input nodes. Code requires both and marks both `required`: 'Your name' (review-client.tsx:209-217) and 'The email this link was sent to' (:218-229); identifyReviewerInput enforces name.trim().min(1,'Tell us your name') and email().max(320) (packages/shared/schemas/reviews.ts:91-95); identifyReviewer additionally rejects any address that is not the invited one (client-review.service.ts:193-201). A TEXT search of the whole of page 1:3 for 'Your name' and 'email this link' returns 0 hits. The canonical page 1:6 draws them: 112:2 'S5.5 · A0 · empty' carries both strings — so this board is a lossy echo, not a design gap.
fix: Port the two FormField groups from 112:2 into the 132px gap in card 1339:7166. Same for the CTA label position.

finding: 'Yes, approve' can fail silently — resolve's error is rendered nowhere, so a client whose round closed elsewhere sees the button flicker and is told nothing.
evidence: resolveReviewByToken throws ALREADY_RESOLVED when status !== PENDING (client-review.service.ts:278-280); the router translates it to CONFLICT with cause.reason (client-review.ts:51-52, :64) and the resolve procedure is wired (:121-127). review-client.tsx renders identify.error (:230-232) and comment.error (:353-355, :390-396) but has zero references to resolve.error; both resolve.mutate calls pass onSuccess only (:407-415, :424-433). The button re-enables via `disabled={resolve.isPending || comment.isPending}` (:447) with no message. Board 1339:7221's own name already records the cause ('CONFLICT comes from resolveReview, whose error is never rendered') and is marked UNBUILDABLE — the defect is in the code, not the board.
fix: Render resolve.error in the confirm dialog beside the existing comment.error line (review-client.tsx:390-396), keyed on cause.reason so ALREADY_RESOLVED gets DEAD_LINK_COPY.CONFLICT's copy. Board 1339:7221 then becomes buildable and its UNBUILDABLE tag can come off.

finding: The DETACHED band is drawn with a disclosure chevron and count ('2 ›') that the built panel does not have — the group is always expanded and nothing collapses it.
evidence: Board 157:2's Detached band renders '⚠ DETACHED  2 ›', the same affordance as the RESOLVED band below it. In code RESOLVED is a Button with aria-expanded and a Chevron (ReviewTab.tsx:742-757); the detached group is a plain <div className={BAND}> with a count span and no toggle (ReviewTab.tsx:698-706). No board draws a collapsed Detached state either.
fix: Either drop the '›' from 157:2's Detached band, or make the band a Button matching ReviewTab.tsx:742-757 and add the collapsed board.

finding: Four of the twelve legend hotspots on the entry board sit underneath the board's own reply-composer artwork, so the labelled route to those states is covered.
evidence: Direct children of 156:2 with rel geometry: 1669:7199 (older-round) @0,706 140x34 · 1669:7201 (re-send-confirm) @140,706 · 1669:7195 (all-resolved) @0,742 · 1669:7197 (resolved-expanded) @140,742 — all inside 1753:8431 'reply-composer' @0,657 280x123, which is later in the child list and therefore above them in z-order. 1138:13542 (loading) @0,774 280x34 is half-covered by 1753:8437 'btn/Revoke link' @0,780 91x32. Every one of those five destinations stays reachable through the frame-level chain (156:2 → 157:58 → 158:2 …), so this is legibility, not reachability. NOT VERIFIED: whether Figma hit-tests a fill-less FRAME in prototype mode — the overlap and z-order are measured, the click outcome is not.
fix: Move the six hotspot chips in the y706-808 band below the 812px board edge, alongside the row already at y820.

finding: 'Note to the reviewer' is collected from the designer, validated, stored and shipped to the client's browser — then rendered by nothing. No client board draws it either.
evidence: SendForReview collects it (SendForReview.tsx:206-217) and passes it as `note` (:112-117); submitReviewInput declares note: z.string().max(500).optional() (packages/shared/schemas/reviews.ts:51); review.service.ts persists it (:65); getReviewByToken returns it in the payload (client-review.service.ts:149). review-client.tsx renders data.changeSummary in the 'What's new' band (:309-313) and never references data.note — grep returns zero hits. Boards 1339:7171 and 1340:7162 draw no note band.
fix: Render data.note under the 'What's new' band in review-client.tsx:309-313 (labelled as a message from the designer, not as a change summary) and draw it on 1339:7171 — or delete the field from SendForReview and the submit schema.

finding: The identify form's error state — the one a client hits by typing the wrong address, which is the only address the link accepts — has no board in this section.
evidence: identifyReviewer throws NOT_INVITED and EMAIL_MISMATCH (client-review.service.ts:193-201), the router deliberately maps both to BAD_REQUEST so the page can show them inline rather than as a dead link (client-review.ts:53-57), and review-client.tsx renders identify.error under the fields (:230-232). Section 1776:8384 has 10 boards, none of them a validation state; the canonical page 1:6 has 112:21 'S5.5 · A0 · validation-error'. The pending label 'One moment…' (review-client.tsx:238) is also undrawn.
fix: Echo 112:21 into section 1776:8384 next to 1339:7162 and wire a hotspot from A0.

finding: The site preview is drawn as one blank rectangle: neither the multi-page tab strip nor the missing-snapshot degradation the code ships has a board.
evidence: SitePreview renders a per-page tab row whenever pages.length > 1, labelling index as 'Home' (review-client.tsx:52-66), and a dashed 'Preview unavailable for this version.' panel when snapshotPages is null (:41-47) — which getReviewByToken produces for any internal submit with no editor render (client-review.service.ts:152-155). Board node 1340:7165 is an empty FRAME named 'Site preview (iframe)' 700x500 with no children; 1339:7171 draws the preview as a caption placeholder. NOT CHECKED: whether page 1:6's 114:2 'S5.5 · commenting' draws either.
fix: Draw the tab strip on 1340:7165 and add a 'preview unavailable' variant board; check 114:2 first in case it already exists to echo.

finding: 'Signed as {Name} · {email}' is missing from the approved and changes-requested boards, although the code prints it on both and one of the two boards asserts in its own name that it does.
evidence: review-client.tsx:269-271 renders `Signed as {data.reviewer!.name} · {data.reviewer!.email}` unconditionally inside the `status !== 'PENDING'` branch, so it appears for APPROVED and CHANGES_REQUESTED alike. Page-1:3 TEXT search for 'Signed as': 1339:7171 (×2, the footer line) and 1340:7174 only. 1339:7186 and 1339:7193 do not draw it — and 1339:7193's board name reads "TERMINAL by design — the branch renders text + 'Signed as', zero controls (review-client.tsx:287-298,247-272)". The canonical 117:58 'S5.5 · approved' on page 1:6 draws it ('Signed as Sara Khan · sara@bellacucina.com').
fix: Copy the 'Signed as' line from 1340:7174 onto 1339:7186 and 1339:7193.

finding: The agency header loses 'is asking for your feedback' on two boards, though the shell renders it in every state.
evidence: Shell's header is one component rendered for every branch, agency name plus the fixed phrase (review-client.tsx:89-92). Board 1339:7163 has both TEXT nodes (1339:7164 '{Agency}', 1339:7165 'is asking for your feedback'); board 1340:7163 has only 1340:7164 '{Agency}'. 1340:7174 (E) is likewise missing it in its screenshot.
fix: Add the second TEXT node to 1340:7163 and to E's header, matching 1339:7163.

finding: The confirm dialog that stands between the client and the signature — the one screen the product exists to collect — is drawn by no board on the echo page or the canonical one.
evidence: review-client.tsx:375-463 renders a full-screen dialog: title 'Approve {siteName}?' / 'Request changes to {siteName}?' (:378-382), body copy that changes on whether a note was typed (:384-389), an inline failure line for the note (:390-396), 'Not yet'/'Go back' (:402) and 'Yes, approve'/'Send and request changes' with three busy labels (:450-458). Both footer buttons only open it (setAsking, :291 and :298) — nothing signs without passing through it. TEXT search for 'Yes, approve', 'Not yet', 'Go back' and 'Send and request': 0 hits on page 1:3, 0 hits on page 1:6.
fix: Draw two variants (approve, request-changes) at the 440px card width the file already uses for confirms, over the A/B shell, and wire 1339:7171's two footer hotspots through it before 1339:7186 / 1339:7193.

finding: Section 18 draws 23 boards for the agency's review panel and not one of them is the state the round ends in — approved.
evidence: TEXT scan of all 23 boards in 1776:8383 for /approv|closed/i returns only: 157:169's round-history rows ('Round 1 · approved 20d ago' etc.), 158:213's toast string 'Review closed — Sara approved v3', and 1717:17235/17246's 'Compare with approved' label. There is no board whose body renders the current round as approved. The nearest thing, 158:213, documents the panel's ABSENCE ('The Review panel is gone. This frame documents the ABSENCE — the panel and the 7th rail icon both disappear when the review closes'), which the code does not do (W-E-01). Ranked worst missing screen in this module: without it there is nothing to build W-E-01's fix against, and nothing for W-E-02's return edge to point at.
fix: Duplicate 157:58 and replace the body with the approved state (who signed, when, and the next move — Publish); decide against 158:213 whether the panel persists or unmounts, and correct 158:213 in the same pass.

finding: CONFIRMED — 'Sent — waiting on your client' appears on no board on page 1:3; so does the bar's other zero-count sentence. The review bar has three count-line branches and one drawn variant.
evidence: ReviewBar.tsx:126-131 selects between `${count} open`, 'Changes requested — nothing left open' and 'Sent — waiting on your client'; the last is reachable and unit-tested (ReviewBar.test.tsx:202). TEXT search across every section of page 1:3: 'waiting on your client' → 0 hits; 'waiting on' → 0; 'Changes requested' as TEXT → 0. A full TEXT dump of 200:213, the bar's own board, gives 200:413 '3 open', 200:414 'Next ›', 200:415 'Compare', 200:417 'Re-send' and the pill 'In review · 3 open' — the count variant only. Also undrawn: 'Re-sending…' (ReviewBar.tsx:157) and the disabled Next ›'s reason 'No open comments to step through' (:140), which is precisely the state that co-occurs with the waiting sentence (count 0 ⇒ open.length 0 ⇒ Next disabled). 200:213 sits in section 01 · Shell, outside this module's two sections — flagged here because the question was asked of this module and the search covered the whole page.
fix: Add two variant boards off 200:213: 'waiting' (sentence in place of the count, Next › disabled with its tooltip) and 'changes-requested' (the other sentence). Owner is the Shell module.

finding: The client page's first two frames — loading, and a load that failed for a reason other than a dead link — have no echo in this section, so the prototype opens straight into a resolved state.
evidence: review-client.tsx:146-154 renders a Shell with agency='Loading' and 'Opening your review…' while clientReview.get is in flight; :159-176 handles review.error, which covers transport failure as well as the four dead-link reasons (the fallback chain ends at DEAD_LINK_COPY.NOT_FOUND at :167). Section 1776:8384's 10 boards are A0, A, B, C, D, E and four dead links — no loading, no generic load-error. Page 1:6 has 121:48 'S5.5 · loading' and 121:25 'S5.5 · load-error'.
fix: Echo 121:48 and 121:25 into 1776:8384 and add hotspots from 1339:7162.

finding: The re-attach board and the built re-attach flow are two different designs, and neither has a board for the other: the file draws a modal picker, the product ships a canvas pick mode.
evidence: Board 184:70 draws 'Re-attach this comment' with the comment quoted, 'Pick the element it should point to now:', three candidate rows and Cancel / Re-attach. In code ReviewTab's Reattach button only emits comments:reattach-start (ReviewTab.tsx:712-719); CommentLayer turns that into a canvas pick — a crosshair overlay (CommentLayer.tsx:414-424), a status pill 'Click an element to re-pin the comment · Esc cancels' (:427-447), a hit-test that toasts 'Pick an element' on a miss (:349-351) and 'Comment re-pinned' on success (:362). No board draws that mode. Board 184:87 'Keep as resolved?' likewise has no code — the detached row's Resolve fires resolveReviewComment immediately with no confirm (ReviewTab.tsx:720, 260-267).
fix: Pick one. If the canvas pick stays, redraw 184:70 as the pick mode (crosshair + status pill on the 1440 shell) and retire the picker modal; 184:87 then either gets built or is retired with it.

finding: Half of the review-closed board's contract describes furniture that was never built: it says a 7th rail icon disappears, and the rail has never had a Review icon.
evidence: 158:213's body TEXT: 'The Review panel is gone. This frame documents the ABSENCE — the panel and the 7th rail icon both disappear when the review closes.' tabsConfig.ts:230-244 defines the review tab with no `zone` and states in its own comment 'the zone-driven rail render leaves it out; the below-divider rail button is a follow-up'. SiteMenu.tsx:50 repeats it: 'The rail has no Review tab either (6 tabs, none of them Review)'. The panel's real doors are the Site menu row (SiteMenu.tsx:203) and the topbar pill CTA (StudioHeader.tsx:662-666 → AquibraStudio.tsx:517) — so this is a stale board claim, not a missing door. The board's other half IS built: the 'Review closed — {who} approved this design.' toast exists (StudioHeader.tsx:292-315) and fires on the transition only.
fix: Rewrite 158:213's body to name the doors that exist (Site menu · Review, topbar pill) and drop the rail-icon sentence — or file the rail button as its own job.

finding: The empty board draws a '0 of 0' progress gauge the code deliberately suppresses — the board is behind a decision already taken and recorded.
evidence: Board 157:221 renders the progress bar with '0 of 0' above 'Sara has not commented yet.'. ReviewTab.tsx:386 gates the whole bar on `total > 0`, with the reason inline at :380-383 ('"0 of 0" over an empty thread was a gauge with no quantity (designer walk 2026-08-28)'). The sent line stays either way. Same class of stale draw as the '‹ ›' round pager and 'Compare with v3' on 156:2 — but those two are already annotated as deliberate deviations in ReviewTab.tsx:25-30 and in 157:169's own caption, and this one is not.
fix: Remove the 0 of 0 bar from 157:221, keeping the 'Sent 2d ago · Sara' line.
